title.zh: 第二十五 百官二 太常 光祿勳 衛尉 太僕 廷尉 大鴻臚
title.raw: 第二十五 百官二 太常 光祿勳 衛尉 太僕 廷尉 大鴻臚 Volume 115: Officials Part Two

sentences.zh: 志第二十五 百官二

translations.literal: Treatise twenty-five: Officials, Part Two.
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 25: Officials, Part Two.

sentences.zh: 太常 光禄勋 卫尉 太仆 廷尉 大鸿胪

translations.literal: Minister of Ceremonies, Minister of the Household, Minister of the Guard, Minister Coachman, Minister of Justice, Grand Herald.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Ceremonies, the Minister of the Household, the Minister of the Guard, the Minister Coachman, the Minister of Justice, and the Grand Herald.

translations.literal: Minister of Ceremonies: minister, one person, at fully ranked two thousand bushels.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Ceremonies: one minister at the top salary grade of two thousand bushels.

translations.literal: Original commentary: he holds rites, protocol, and sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He oversees court ritual, ceremonial protocol, and state sacrifices.

translations.literal: On each sacrifice, he first presents the ritual protocol;
translations.idiomatic: Before every sacrifice he memorializes the order of rites to be observed;

translations.literal: when carrying them out, he constantly assists the Son of Heaven with recitations.
translations.idiomatic: during the rite itself he prompts the emperor with the liturgical responses.

sentences.zh: 汉旧仪曰：「赞飨一人，秩六百石，掌赞天子。」

translations.literal: The Old Han Ceremonies says: "One libation assistant, rank six hundred bushels, masters assisting the Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: The Old Han Ceremonies names one libation assistant at six hundred bushels to prompt the emperor during the feast."

translations.literal: Whenever erudites are selected and examined, he reports whether they are qualified or not.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever erudites sit for promotion or examination, he reports on their competence.

sentences.zh: 大射、养老、大丧，皆奏其礼仪。

translations.literal: For the grand archery, elder nurturing, and great mourning, all he presents their ritual protocols.
translations.idiomatic: The grand archery, the honoring of the aged, and state funerals all require his memorial on correct ritual.

translations.literal: Each month on the last day before the dark moon, he inspects progress at the mausoleums and shrines.
translations.idiomatic: On the eve of each month’s last day he tours the imperial tombs and ancestral shrines to see that all is in order.

translations.literal: One assistant, comparable to one thousand bushels.
translations.idiomatic: He has one assistant at one thousand bushels equivalent.

translations.literal: Six hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: Some registers list that post at six hundred bushels instead.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：掌凡行礼及祭祀小事，总署曹事。

translations.literal: Original commentary: he holds general conduct of rites and small matters of sacrifice, and overall superintends bureau affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The assistant handles routine observances and minor cult matters and coordinates the ministry’s bureaus.

sentences.zh: 汉旧仪曰：「丞举庙中非法者。」

translations.literal: The Old Han Ceremonies says: "The assistant reports unlawful conduct in the shrine."
translations.idiomatic: The Old Han Ceremonies requires the assistant to report ritual violations in the ancestral shrine."

sentences.zh: 其署曹掾史，随事为员，诸卿皆然。

translations.literal: As for the bureau attendants and clerks in his office, according to affairs they make up the quota; all the ministers are thus.
translations.idiomatic: Bureau staff numbers flex with the workload; the same rule applies across the nine ministers.

translations.literal: Director of Astronomy, one person, six hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: One Director of Astronomy at six hundred bushels.

translations.literal: Original commentary: he holds seasons and weather, stars and calendars.
translations.idiomatic: He watches the seasons, weather patterns, stars, and the civil calendar.

translations.literal: Whenever the year is about to end, he presents the calendar for the new year.
translations.idiomatic: At year’s end he presents the almanac for the coming year.

sentences.zh: 凡国祭祀、丧、娶之事，掌奏良日及时节禁忌。

translations.literal: For state sacrifices, mourning, and marriage matters, he presents auspicious days and timely prohibitions.
translations.idiomatic: For state sacrifices, funerals, and royal weddings he proposes lucky dates and seasonal taboos.

sentences.zh: 凡国有瑞应、灾异，掌记之。

translations.literal: For state prodigies of auspicious response and disasters or anomalies, he records them.
translations.idiomatic: He logs auspicious omens and ill portents for the archives.

sentences.zh: 汉官曰：「太史待诏三十七人，其六人治历，三人龟卜，三人庐宅，四人日时，三人易筮，二人典禳，九人籍氏、许氏、典昌氏，各三人，嘉法、请雨、解事各二人，医一人。」

translations.literal: The Offices of Han says: "Thirty-seven awaiting-edict officers of the Director of Astronomy: six manage calendars, three turtle divination, three house-site divination, four day-and-time, three Changes divination, two exorcism, nine of the Ji, Xu, and Dianchang clans three each, auspicious methods, rain prayers, and case resolution two each, one physician."
translations.idiomatic: The Offices of Han assigns thirty-seven awaiting-edict astronomers to calendars, divination, timing, exorcism, clan specialists, rain prayers, case work, and one court physician."

translations.literal: One assistant.
translations.idiomatic: He has one assistant.

sentences.zh: 明堂及灵台丞一人，二百石。

translations.literal: Assistant for the Bright Hall and Spiritual Terrace, one person, two hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: One deputy for the Bright Hall and Spiritual Terrace at two hundred bushels.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：二丞，掌守明堂、灵台。

translations.literal: Original commentary: the two assistants guard the Bright Hall and Spiritual Terrace.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: paired deputies keep watch over the Bright Hall and Spiritual Terrace.

sentences.zh: 灵台掌候日月星气，皆属太史。

translations.literal: The Spiritual Terrace masters observing sun, moon, stars, and vapors; all belong to the Director of Astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: The Spiritual Terrace tracks sun, moon, stars, and ether—all under the Director of Astronomy.

sentences.zh: 汉官曰：「灵台待诏四十一人，其十四人候星，二人候日，三人候风，十二人候气，三人候晷景，七人候钟律。

translations.literal: The Offices of Han says: "Forty-one awaiting-edict officers at the Spiritual Terrace: fourteen observe stars, two observe the sun, three observe wind, twelve observe vapors, three observe gnomon shadows, seven observe pitch pipes and measures.
translations.idiomatic: The Offices of Han says: "Forty-one Spiritual Terrace awaiting-edict officers: fourteen for stars, two for the sun, three for wind, twelve for vapors, three for sundials, seven for pitch pipes,

translations.literal: One attendant."
translations.idiomatic: and one attendant."

translations.literal: Erudite libationer, one person, six hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: One erudite libationer at six hundred bushels.

translations.literal: Originally Erudite Pushe; at restoration changed to libationer.
translations.idiomatic: The head of the erudites was originally titled Pushe; after the restoration the office was renamed libationer (jijiu).

sentences.zh: 胡广曰：「官名祭酒，皆一位之元长者也。

translations.literal: Hu Guang said: "The office title libationer designates the senior head of a single rank.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Guang explained: "The title jijiu marks the senior head of a bureau.

sentences.zh: 古礼，宾客得主人馔，则老者一人举酒以祭于地，旧说以为示有先。」

translations.literal: In ancient ritual, when guests received food from the host, the eldest among them would raise wine and offer it to the ground; older explanations hold that this showed regard for ancestors."
translations.idiomatic: In ancient guest ritual the eldest would pour a libation to the ground to honor those who came before."

translations.literal: Fourteen erudites, comparable to six hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: Fourteen court erudites at six hundred bushels equivalent.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：《易》四，施、孟、梁丘、京氏。

translations.literal: Original commentary: for the Changes, four traditions: Shi, Meng, Liangqiu, and Jing.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes is taught in four schools—Shi, Meng, Liangqiu, and Jing.

translations.literal: For the Documents, three: Ouyang, Greater and Lesser Xiahou.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents has three lines—Ouyang and the elder and younger Xiahou traditions.

translations.literal: For the Odes, three: Lu, Qi, and Han.
translations.idiomatic: The Odes are represented by the Lu, Qi, and Han schools.

translations.literal: For the Rites, two: Greater and Lesser Dai.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites survive in the elder and younger Dai recensions.

translations.literal: For the Spring and Autumn, two: the Gongyang traditions of Yan and Yan.
translations.idiomatic: The Spring and Autumn is taught in two Gongyang schools, the lineages of Master Yan Pengzu and Master Yan Anle.

translations.literal: They master teaching disciples.
translations.idiomatic: They instruct the disciples enrolled at the academy.

translations.literal: When the state has doubtful matters, they undertake to answer inquiries.
translations.idiomatic: When policy questions arise, they supply learned answers on demand.

translations.literal: Originally four hundred bushels; Emperor Xuan increased the rank.
translations.idiomatic: Their stipend began at four hundred bushels until Emperor Xuan raised it.

translations.literal: Director of Invocations, one person, six hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: One Director of Invocations at six hundred bushels.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：凡国祭祀，掌读祝及迎送神。

translations.literal: Original commentary: for state sacrifices, he reads invocations and welcomes and sends off the spirits.
translations.idiomatic: At state sacrifices he chants the prayer texts and conducts the spirits’ arrival and departure.

sentences.zh: 汉旧仪曰：「庙祭，太祝令主席酒。」

translations.literal: The Old Han Ceremonies says: "At shrine sacrifice, the Director of Invocations presides over the libation wine."
translations.idiomatic: The Old Han Ceremonies makes the Director of Invocations preside over the libation at ancestral rites."

sentences.zh: 汉官曰：「员吏四十一人，其二人百石，二人斗食，二十二人佐，二人学事，四人守学事，九人有秩。

translations.literal: The Offices of Han says: "Forty-one staff: two at one hundred bushels, two at dou-food rank, twenty-two assistants, two student clerks, four supervising student clerks, nine with stipends.
translations.idiomatic: The Offices of Han says: "Forty-one clerks

sentences.zh: 百五十人祝人，宰二百四十二人，屠者六十人。」

translations.literal: One hundred fifty invokers, two hundred forty-two butchers, sixty slaughterers."
translations.idiomatic: plus 150 invokers, 242 butchers, and 60 slaughterers for the shrine staff."

translations.literal: One assistant.
translations.idiomatic: He has one assistant.

translations.literal: Original commentary: he masters invocation of lesser deity affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The assistant tends invocations to secondary cults.

translations.literal: Director of the Grand Butcher, one person, six hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: One Director of the Grand Butcher at six hundred bushels.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：掌宰工鼎俎馔具之物。

translations.literal: Original commentary: he holds butcher-craftsmen, tripods, meat stands, and prepared offerings.
translations.idiomatic: He supervised butchers, vessels, and sacrificial food preparations.

translations.literal: For state sacrifices, he masters arranging prepared offerings.
translations.idiomatic: At state sacrifices he arranged the food offerings.

sentences.zh: 汉官曰：「明堂丞一人，二百石。

translations.literal: The Offices of Han says: "One Bright Hall assistant at two hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: The Offices of Han says: "The Bright Hall has one two-hundred-bushel assistant,

sentences.zh: 员吏四十二人，其二人百石，二人斗食，二十三人佐，九人有秩，二人学事，四人守学事。

translations.literal: Forty-two staff: two at one hundred bushels, two at dou-food rank, twenty-three assistants, nine with stipends, two student clerks, four supervising student clerks.
translations.idiomatic: forty-two clerks,

sentences.zh: 宰二百四十二人，屠者七十三人，卫士一十五人。」

translations.literal: Two hundred forty-two butchers, seventy-three slaughterers, fifteen guards."
translations.idiomatic: 242 butchers, 73 slaughterers, and 15 guards."

translations.literal: One assistant.
translations.idiomatic: He has one assistant.

sentences.zh: 大予乐令一人，本注曰：掌伎乐。

translations.literal: Director of the Grand Imperial Music, one person; original commentary: he holds performances and music.
translations.idiomatic: One Director of Grand Imperial Music, charged with court performance and ritual music.

sentences.zh: 凡国祭祀，掌请奏乐，及大飨用乐，掌其陈序。

translations.literal: For state sacrifices, he requests and presents music; for great feasts using music, he holds their arrangement and order.
translations.idiomatic: He schedules music at sacrifices and arranges the program for great banquets that include orchestral performance.

translations.literal: One assistant.
translations.idiomatic: He has one assistant.

translations.literal: Gaozu’s shrine director, one person, six hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: One keeper of Emperor Gaozu’s shrine at six hundred bushels.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：守庙，掌案行扫除。

translations.literal: Original commentary: guards the shrine; masters inspection tours and sweeping.
translations.idiomatic: He tends the shrine, inspects its precincts, and keeps them swept.

translations.literal: No assistant.
translations.idiomatic: There is no deputy to this office.

translations.literal: Founding Ancestor’s shrine director, one person, six hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: One keeper of Guangwu’s shrine at six hundred bushels.

translations.literal: Original commentary: as for Gaozu’s shrine.
translations.idiomatic: His duties mirror those at Gaozu’s shrine.

sentences.zh: 汉官曰：「员吏六人，卫士二十人。」

translations.literal: The Offices of Han says: "Six staff and twenty guards."
translations.idiomatic: The Offices of Han lists six clerks and twenty guards."

sentences.zh: 先帝陵，每陵园令各一人，六百石。

translations.literal: For former emperors' mausoleums, each mausoleum park has one director, six hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: Each deceased emperor's mausoleum park had one director at six hundred bushels.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：掌守陵园，案行扫除。

translations.literal: Original commentary: he holds guarding the mausoleum park and inspects sweeping and cleaning.
translations.idiomatic: He keeps the mausoleum grounds and inspects sweeping and upkeep.

translations.literal: One assistant and one commandant each.
translations.idiomatic: Each park has one assistant and one camp commandant.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：校长，主兵戎盗贼事。

translations.literal: Original commentary: the commandant masters weapons, troops, bandits, and thieves.
translations.idiomatic: The commandant handles armed watch and suppresses banditry within the park.

sentences.zh: 先帝陵，每陵食官令各一人，六百石。

translations.literal: For former emperors’ mausoleums, each mausoleum has one granary director, six hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: Each imperial tomb also has a granary director at six hundred bushels for offerings.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：掌望晦时节祭祀。

translations.literal: Original commentary: masters new-moon and dark-moon seasonal sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: He presides over the monthly offering rites at the new and dark moons.

translations.literal: Those on the right belong to the Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: The offices listed at right fall under the Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：有祠祀令一人，后转属少府。

translations.literal: Original commentary: there was one director of shrine offerings, later transferred to the Minister of the Lesser Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: There used to be a director of shrine offerings; that post was later moved to the Minister of the Lesser Treasury.

sentences.zh: 有太卜令，六百石，后省并太史。

translations.literal: There was a director of grand divination, six hundred bushels; later abolished and merged into the Director of Astronomy.
translations.idiomatic: The old Director of Grand Divination at six hundred bushels was cut and folded into the Director of Astronomy.

translations.literal: Since the restoration, ten offices in all from before were eliminated.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Eastern restoration, ten Western Han offices in this ministry have been abolished.

sentences.zh: 案前书，十官者，太宰、均官、都水、雍太祝、五畤各一尉也。

translations.literal: According to the Former Book, the ten offices were: Grand Butcher, Equalization, Capital Waters, Yong Grand Invocator, and Five Altars—each with one commandant.
translations.idiomatic: The Former Book lists ten offices—Grand Butcher, Equalization, Capital Waters, Yong Grand Invocator, and the Five Altars—each with its own commandant.

sentences.zh: 东观书曰：「章帝又置祀令、丞，延平元年省。」

translations.literal: The Eastern Lodge Record says: "Emperor Zhang also set up directors and assistants of sacrifices; they were abolished in the first year of Yanping."
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Lodge Record notes that Emperor Zhang added sacrifice directors, cut in Yanping 1."

sentences.zh: 光禄勋，卿一人，中二千石。

translations.literal: Minister of the Household, minister, one person, at fully ranked two thousand bushels.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of the Household: one minister at fully ranked two thousand bushels.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：掌宿卫宫殿门户，典谒署郎更直执戟，宿卫门户，考其德行而进退之。

translations.literal: Original commentary: he holds night-watch at palace gates and doors, manages reception offices and gentlemen-of-the-house in rotating watch bearing halberds, night-watch at gates and doors, examines their conduct and virtue and promotes or demotes them.
translations.idiomatic: He commands palace gate security, runs the audience bureaus, and rotates gentlemen-of-the-house on halberd watch while judging their conduct for promotion or dismissal.

sentences.zh: 胡广曰：「勋犹门昏也，易曰『为门昏寺』。

translations.literal: Hu Guang said: "Xun means gate-ward, as the Changes says 'he made gate-ward temples.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Guang derived xun from gate-warding, citing the Changes line on gate temples;

translations.literal: Eunuch temples master the duty of palace gates and doors."
translations.idiomatic: the palace eunuch bureaus guarded the palace gates."

translations.literal: In suburban sacrifice affairs, he presents the three libations.
translations.idiomatic: At suburban sacrifices he presents the three ritual libations of wine.

translations.literal: One assistant, comparable to one thousand bushels.
translations.idiomatic: He has one assistant at one thousand bushels equivalent.

sentences.zh: 五官中郎将一人，比二千石。

translations.literal: Leader of gentlemen-of-the-house for the five offices, one person, comparable to two thousand bushels.
translations.idiomatic: One captain of the central gentlemen for the five bureaus at two thousand bushels equivalent.

translations.literal: Original commentary: he commands the gentlemen for the five offices.
translations.idiomatic: He leads the gentlemen attached to the five ministries.

translations.literal: Gentlemen of the house for the five offices at middle rank, comparable to six hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: Central gentlemen for the five bureaus at six hundred bushels equivalent.

translations.literal: Original commentary: no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: There is no statutory head count.

sentences.zh: 胡广曰：「光禄大夫，本为中大夫，武帝元狩五年置谏大夫为光禄大夫，世祖中兴，以为谏议大夫。

translations.literal: Hu Guang said: "The Household Grandee was originally Middle Grandee. In the fifth year of Yuanshou under Emperor Wu remonstrating grandees were made household grandees; at Emperor Guangwu's restoration they became remonstrating grandees.
translations.idiomatic: Hu Guang said: "The Household Grandee was originally the Middle Grandee; in the fifth year of Yuanshou under Emperor Wu remonstrating grandees were made household grandees, and at Guangwu's restoration they became remonstrating grandees.

translations.literal: There were also grandees within the palace and grandees of scattered attendance.
translations.idiomatic: alongside palace and scattered grandees

sentences.zh: 此四等于古皆为天子之下大夫，视列国之上卿。」

translations.literal: These four grades in antiquity were all the Son of Heaven's lower grandees, equivalent to the upper ministers of feudal states."
translations.idiomatic: —four grades matching the ancient lower grandees of the ruler."

translations.literal: The Offices of Han says thirty men.
translations.idiomatic: The Offices of Han sets the quota at thirty.

sentences.zh: 郎年五十以屬五官，故曰六百石。

translations.literal: Gentlemen aged fifty were attached to the Five Offices, so they were said to be six hundred shi.
translations.idiomatic: Gentlemen aged fifty were attached to the Five Offices, so they were said to be six hundred shi.

translations.literal: Gentlemen attendants for the five offices, comparable to four hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant gentlemen for the five bureaus at four hundred bushels equivalent.

translations.literal: Original commentary: no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: There is no statutory head count.

translations.literal: Gentlemen secretaries for the five offices, comparable to three hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: Secretary gentlemen for the five bureaus at three hundred bushels equivalent.

translations.literal: Original commentary: no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: There is no statutory head count.

sentences.zh: 凡郎官皆主更直执戟，宿卫诸殿门，出充车骑。

translations.literal: All gentlemen-of-the-house chiefly rotate watch bearing halberds, night-watch at the various hall gates, and go out to act as chariots and cavalry escort.
translations.idiomatic: Gentlemen-of-the-house stand rotating halberd watch at palace doors and ride out as imperial escort.

translations.literal: Only advisory gentlemen are not in the watch rotation.
translations.idiomatic: Advisory gentlemen alone are exempt from guard duty.

translations.literal: Left leader of gentlemen-of-the-house at middle rank, comparable to two thousand bushels.
translations.idiomatic: The left captain of the central gentlemen at two thousand bushels equivalent.

translations.literal: Original commentary: he commands gentlemen of the left bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He commands gentlemen of the left wing.

translations.literal: Gentlemen at middle rank, comparable to six hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: Central gentlemen at six hundred bushels equivalent.

translations.literal: Gentlemen attendants, comparable to four hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant gentlemen at four hundred bushels equivalent.

translations.literal: Gentlemen secretaries, comparable to three hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: Secretary gentlemen at three hundred bushels equivalent.

translations.literal: Three gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Three gentlemen.

translations.literal: Original commentary: all have no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: Again, no statutory quotas.

translations.literal: Right leader of gentlemen-of-the-house at middle rank, comparable to two thousand bushels.
translations.idiomatic: The right captain of the central gentlemen at two thousand bushels equivalent.

translations.literal: Original commentary: he commands gentlemen of the right bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He commands gentlemen of the right wing.

translations.literal: Gentlemen at middle rank, comparable to six hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: Central gentlemen at six hundred bushels equivalent.

translations.literal: Gentlemen attendants, comparable to four hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant gentlemen at four hundred bushels equivalent.

translations.literal: Gentlemen secretaries, comparable to three hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: Secretary gentlemen at three hundred bushels equivalent.

translations.literal: Original commentary: all have no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: Again, no statutory quotas.

translations.literal: The three corps of gentlemen all have no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: All three gentleman corps lacked fixed quotas.

translations.literal: Leader of gentlemen-of-the-house for the tiger-rank bodyguard, comparable to two thousand bushels.
translations.idiomatic: The captain of the household rapid guard at two thousand bushels equivalent.

translations.literal: Original commentary: he commands tiger-rank bodyguard night-watch.
translations.idiomatic: He leads the rapid guards who stand night watch at close quarters.

sentences.zh: 前书武帝置期门，平帝更名虎贲。

translations.literal: The Former Book says Emperor Wu set up the Gate of Expected Arrival; Emperor Ping renamed it Tiger-Rank Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The Former Book records that Emperor Wu created the Gate of Expected Arrival and Emperor Ping renamed it the rapid guard.

sentences.zh: 蔡质汉仪曰：「主虎贲千五百人，无常员，多至千人。

translations.literal: Cai Zhi's Han Ceremonies says: "They command one thousand five hundred tiger-rank guards, no fixed quota, often up to one thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Zhi's Han Ceremonies says: "They command 1,500 rapid guards, without a fixed quota, often up to a thousand.

translations.literal: They wear pheasant caps and rank next to the right general's bureau."
translations.idiomatic: wearing pheasant caps and quartered next to the right general's office."

sentences.zh: 又虎贲旧作「虎奔」，言如虎之奔也，王莽以古有勇士孟贲，故名焉。

translations.literal: Formerly hu-ben was written "tiger-run," meaning to run like a tiger; Wang Mang, because antiquity had the warrior Meng Ben, therefore gave the name.
translations.idiomatic: The name was once written "tiger-run" for swiftness; Wang Mang linked it to the ancient warrior Meng Ben.

sentences.zh: 孔安国曰「若虎贲兽」，言其甚猛。

translations.literal: Kong Anguo said "like the tiger-rank beast," meaning they are very fierce.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Anguo said they were "like tiger-rank beasts," meaning they were very fierce.

sentences.zh: 左右仆射、左右陛长各一人，比六百石。

translations.literal: Left and right shooting supervisors and left and right stairhead captains, one each, comparable to six hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: Left and right adjutants and left and right stair captains—one of each at six hundred bushels equivalent.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：仆射，主虎贲郎习射。

translations.literal: Original commentary: shooting supervisors command tiger-rank gentlemen in archery practice.
translations.idiomatic: The adjutants drill the rapid guard in archery.

sentences.zh: 陛长，主直虎贲，朝会在殿中。

translations.literal: Stairhead captains command watch-standing tiger-rank guards; at court assemblies they are in the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Stair captains post rapid guards inside the hall during audiences.

translations.literal: The Offices of Han says: "Stairhead captains, black ribbon and bronze seal."
translations.idiomatic: The Offices of Han gives stair captains black ribbons and bronze seals."

translations.literal: Tiger-rank gentlemen at middle rank, comparable to six hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: Rapid-guard central gentlemen at six hundred bushels equivalent.

translations.literal: Tiger-rank gentlemen attendants, comparable to four hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: Rapid-guard attendant gentlemen at four hundred bushels equivalent.

translations.literal: Tiger-rank gentlemen secretaries, comparable to three hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: Rapid-guard secretary gentlemen at three hundred bushels equivalent.

sentences.zh: 荀绰晋百官表注曰：「虎贲诸郎，皆父死子代，汉制也。」

translations.literal: Xun Chuo's Jin Table of Offices commentary says: "All tiger-rank gentlemen succeed father to son; this is Han institution."
translations.idiomatic: Xun Chuo noted that rapid-guard gentlemen inherited from father to son under Han rule."

translations.literal: Halberd-following tiger-rank guards, comparable to two hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: Halberd-bearing rapid guards at two hundred bushels equivalent.

translations.literal: Four corps of gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Four gentleman corps.

translations.literal: Original commentary: all have no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: Again, no statutory quotas.

translations.literal: They hold night-watch attendance and following.
translations.idiomatic: They provide close escort and night security for the throne.

sentences.zh: 自节从虎贲久者转迁，才能差高至中郎。

translations.literal: From halberd-following tiger-rank guards, those long in service transfer and advance; according to ability, somewhat higher reach middle gentlemen rank.
translations.idiomatic: Veterans of the halberd-bearing guard rotate upward, and the abler among them may rise to central gentleman.

translations.literal: Leader of gentlemen-of-the-house for the feathered forest, comparable to two thousand bushels.
translations.idiomatic: The captain of the Feathered Forest guard at two thousand bushels equivalent.

translations.literal: Original commentary: he commands feathered-forest gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: He commands the Feathered Forest gentlemen.

translations.literal: Feathered-forest gentlemen, comparable to three hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: Feathered Forest gentlemen at three hundred bushels equivalent.

translations.literal: Original commentary: no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: There is no statutory head count.

translations.literal: They hold night-watch attendance and following.
translations.idiomatic: They provide close escort and night security for the throne.

sentences.zh: 常选汉阳、陇西、安定、北地、上郡、西河凡六郡良家补。

translations.literal: They are regularly selected from the six commanderies Hanyang, Longxi, Anding, Beidi, Shangjun, and Xihe, good families to fill the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Recruits are drawn in rotation from respectable households across six northwestern commanderies.

sentences.zh: 本武帝以便马从猎，还宿殿陛巖下室中，故号巖郎。

translations.literal: Originally Emperor Wu used nimble mounts to follow the hunt, returning to lodge in the chamber beneath the palace steps, therefore they were called “step-gentlemen.”
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu first rode light mounts on the hunt and billeted his escort under the hall steps, whence the nickname “gallery guard.”

sentences.zh: 前书曰初置名建章营骑，后更名。

translations.literal: The Former Book says at first they were set up as Jianzhang camp cavalry, later renamed.
translations.idiomatic: The Former Book records that the corps was first titled Jianzhang camp cavalry and later renamed.

translations.literal: On leaving service they are supplemented as three-hundred-bushel assistants and commandants.
translations.idiomatic: Veterans were posted out as three-hundred-bushel assistants and commandants.

sentences.zh: 荀绰晋百官表注曰：「言其严厉整锐也。」

translations.literal: Xun Chuo's Jin Table of Offices commentary says: "This means stern, severe, and sharp."
translations.idiomatic: Xun Chuo glossed the name as denoting stern discipline and sharp readiness."

sentences.zh: 案此则为岩郎，与志不同。

translations.literal: On investigation this refers to gallery gentlemen, differing from the treatise.
translations.idiomatic: This account treats them as gallery guards, which differs from the treatise elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 蔡质汉仪曰：「羽林郎百二十八人，无常员，府次虎贲府。」

translations.literal: Cai Zhi's Han Ceremonies says: "One hundred twenty-eight Feathered Forest gentlemen, no fixed quota; the bureau ranks next to the Tiger-Rank Guard bureau."
translations.idiomatic: Cai Zhi's Han Ceremonies says: "128 Feathered Forest gentlemen without a fixed quota, quartered next to the rapid guard."

translations.literal: Left superintendent of the Feathered Forest, one person, six hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: One left superintendent of the Feathered Forest at six hundred bushels.

translations.literal: Original commentary: he commands the Feathered Forest left cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He commands the left wing of Feathered Forest cavalry.

translations.literal: One assistant.
translations.idiomatic: He has one assistant.

translations.literal: Right superintendent of the Feathered Forest, one person, six hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: One right superintendent of the Feathered Forest at six hundred bushels.

translations.literal: Original commentary: he commands the Feathered Forest right cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: He commands the right wing of Feathered Forest cavalry.

translations.literal: One assistant.
translations.idiomatic: He has one assistant.

translations.literal: Commandant of the imperial chariot, comparable to two thousand bushels.
translations.idiomatic: Commandants of the imperial chariot at two thousand bushels equivalent.

translations.literal: Original commentary: no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: There is no statutory head count.

translations.literal: He holds the imperial carriage and chariots.
translations.idiomatic: They drive and maintain the emperor’s traveling carriages.

translations.literal: Commandant of the horse escort, comparable to two thousand bushels.
translations.idiomatic: Commandants of the horse escort at two thousand bushels equivalent.

translations.literal: Original commentary: no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: There is no statutory head count.

translations.literal: The Offices of Han says five men.
translations.idiomatic: The Offices of Han sets the quota at five.

translations.literal: He holds the horse escort.
translations.idiomatic: He commands the emperor's horse escort.

translations.literal: Commandant of cavalry, comparable to two thousand bushels.
translations.idiomatic: Commandants of cavalry at two thousand bushels equivalent.

translations.literal: Original commentary: no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: There is no statutory head count.

translations.literal: Originally they supervised Feathered Forest cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: The post originally oversaw Feathered Forest mounted troops.

translations.literal: Household grandee, comparable to two thousand bushels.
translations.idiomatic: Household grandees at two thousand bushels equivalent.

translations.literal: Original commentary: no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: There is no statutory head count.

sentences.zh: 凡大夫、议郎皆掌顾问应对，无常事，唯诏令所使。

translations.literal: As for grandees and advisory gentlemen, all hold counsel and response; there are no constant duties; only as edicts and orders dispatch them.
translations.idiomatic: Household grandees and advisory gentlemen serve as ad hoc consultants, with no standing portfolio beyond what an edict assigns.

sentences.zh: 凡诸国嗣之丧，则光禄大夫掌吊。

translations.literal: Whenever feudal states’ heirs die, then the household grandee masters condolence missions.
translations.idiomatic: When a feudal heir dies, a household grandee leads the court’s mission of condolence.

translations.literal: Grandee within the palace, one thousand bushels.
translations.idiomatic: Grandees within the palace at one thousand bushels.

translations.literal: Original commentary: no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: There is no statutory head count.

translations.literal: Grandee of scattered attendance, six hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: Grandees of scattered attendance at six hundred bushels.

translations.literal: Original commentary: no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: There is no statutory head count.

translations.literal: Grandee remonstrant, six hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrating grandees at six hundred bushels.

translations.literal: Original commentary: no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: There is no statutory head count.

sentences.zh: 议郎，六百石，本注曰：无员。

translations.literal: Advisory gentleman, six hundred bushels; original commentary: no fixed quota.
translations.idiomatic: Advisory gentlemen at six hundred bushels, without a statutory quota.

translations.literal: The Offices of Han says: "Fifty men, no fixed quota."
translations.idiomatic: The Offices of Han lists fifty men without a fixed quota."

translations.literal: Shepherd of receptionists, one person, comparable to one thousand bushels.
translations.idiomatic: One chief receptionist at one thousand bushels equivalent.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：为谒者台率，主谒者，天子出，奉引。

translations.literal: Original commentary: he is leader of the receptionists' bureau, commands receptionists; when the Son of Heaven goes out, he leads the procession.
translations.idiomatic: He heads the reception corps, and when the emperor leaves the palace he leads the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 古重习武，有主射以督录之。

translations.literal: In antiquity they valued martial practice; there was a master of archery to supervise and record them.
translations.idiomatic: Antiquity prized martial drill; a master archer supervised the corps.

translations.literal: Therefore it is called "shepherd" (pushe).
translations.idiomatic: Hence the title pushe, "shepherd of archers."

sentences.zh: 蔡质汉仪曰：「见尚书令，对揖无敬。

translations.literal: Cai Zhi's Han Ceremonies says: "When meeting the Master of Writing, they bow facing each other without full obeisance.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Zhi's Han Ceremonies says: "When they meet the Master of Writing, they exchange bows without full prostration,

translations.literal: When receptionists meet, they hold the tablet and bow."
translations.idiomatic: but bowed with tablets to receptionists."

sentences.zh: 常侍谒者五人，比六百石。

translations.literal: Constant attendant receptionists, five persons, comparable to six hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: Five standing receptionists at six hundred bushels equivalent.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：主殿上时节威仪。

translations.literal: Original commentary: they hold seasonal order and ceremony on the hall above.
translations.idiomatic: They regulate ritual pacing and demeanor during audiences.

translations.literal: Thirty receptionists.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty receptionists serve in rotation.

translations.literal: Those who are serving receptionists, four hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: Serving receptionists draw four hundred bushels.

sentences.zh: 其灌谒者郎中，比三百石。

translations.literal: Those who are bathed receptionists and gentlemen secretaries, comparable to three hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: Bathed receptionists acting as gentleman secretaries rank at three hundred bushels equivalent.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：掌宾赞受事，及上章报问。

translations.literal: Original commentary: they hold guest protocol, receiving business, and submitting memorials and answering inquiries.
translations.idiomatic: They greet envoys, take in petitions, and carry answers back to supplicants.

sentences.zh: 将、大夫以下之丧，掌使吊。

translations.literal: For mourning of generals and grandees downward, they are dispatched to offer condolence.
translations.idiomatic: They carry the court’s condolences to the funerals of generals and officials of lower rank.

sentences.zh: 本员七十人，中兴但三十人。

translations.literal: Originally the quota was seventy persons; at restoration only thirty.
translations.idiomatic: Western Han filled seventy slots; the restored court cut the corps to thirty.

sentences.zh: 荀绰晋百官表注曰：「汉皆用孝廉年五十，威容严恪能宾者为之。

translations.literal: Xun Chuo's Jin Table of Offices commentary says: "Han always appointed filial and incorrupt men aged fifty, of stern bearing and dignified manner able to receive guests.
translations.idiomatic: Xun Chuo's Jin commentary on the offices says: "Han chose fifty-year-old filial and incorrupt men of grave bearing to serve as receptionists.

sentences.zh: 明帝诏曰：『谒者乃尧之尊官，所以试舜宾于四门，四门穆穆者也。』

translations.literal: Emperor Ming's edict said: 'Receptionists were Yao's honored office, by which Shun was tested as guest at the four gates, and the four gates were reverent.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming called the post one of Yao's great offices, the office that tested Shun at the four gates.

sentences.zh: 昔燕太子使荆轲劫始皇，变起两楹之间，其后谒者持匕首刺腋，高祖偃武行文，故易之以板。」

translations.literal: Formerly the crown prince of Yan sent Jing Ke to seize the First Emperor; the crisis arose between the two pillars, and afterward a receptionist stabbed him in the armpit with a dagger. Emperor Gaozu laid aside arms and promoted culture, and therefore replaced daggers with tablets."
translations.idiomatic: Formerly the crown prince of Yan sent Jing Ke to seize the First Emperor; the crisis arose between the two pillars, and afterward receptionists carried daggers at the armpit. Gaozu laid aside arms and promoted culture, and therefore replaced them with tablets."

sentences.zh: 初为灌谒者，满岁为给事谒者。

translations.literal: At first they are bathed receptionists; when a full year is complete they become serving receptionists.
translations.idiomatic: A novice begins as a bathed receptionist and after one year graduates to serving receptionist.

sentences.zh: 蔡质汉仪曰：「出府丞、长史、陵令，皆选仪容端正，任奉使者。」

translations.literal: Cai Zhi's Han Ceremonies says: "For outgoing bureau assistants, chief clerks, and mausoleum directors, all are chosen for proper bearing and appearance, appointed as envoys on mission."
translations.idiomatic: Cai Zhi required handsome, dignified men for assistants, chief clerks, and mausoleum directors sent out as envoys."

translations.literal: Those on the right belong to the Minister of the Household.
translations.idiomatic: The offices at right fall under the Minister of the Household.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：职属光禄者，自五官将至羽林右监，凡七署。

translations.literal: Original commentary: offices subordinate to the Household, from the leader of gentlemen for the five offices down to the right superintendent of the Feathered Forest, in all seven bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Household-line commands run from the captain of the five bureaus through the right Feathered Forest superintendent—seven bureaus in all.

sentences.zh: 自奉车都尉至谒者，以文属焉。

translations.literal: From commandant of the imperial chariot down to receptionists, by civil subordination they attach there.
translations.idiomatic: From chariot commandants through receptionists they count as civil adjuncts of the same ministry.

sentences.zh: 旧有左右曹，秩以二千石，上殿中，主受尚书奏事，平省之。

translations.literal: Formerly there were left and right Cao at two-thousand-bushel rank, ascending to the hall, receiving Masters of Writing memorials and leveling and reviewing them.
translations.idiomatic: Western Han also posted left and right palace secretaries at two thousand bushels to take memorials from the Masters of Writing for screening inside the hall.

sentences.zh: 世祖省，使小黄门郎受事，车驾出，给黄门郎兼。

translations.literal: The Founding Ancestor eliminated them, having petty gentlemen of the Yellow Gate receive business; when the chariot goes out, petty gentlemen of the Yellow Gate double in the duty.
translations.idiomatic: Guangwu abolished those posts and had petty Yellow Gate gentlemen handle intake; on imperial progresses those same gentlemen double as escort.

sentences.zh: 有请室令，车驾出，在前请所幸，徼车迎白，示重慎。

translations.literal: There was a director of the petition chamber; when the chariot went out, he went ahead to request the intended destination, patrol chariots met him with the report, showing gravity and caution.
translations.idiomatic: A director of the petition chamber once rode ahead to learn the emperor’s intended route so patrol cars could announce it—an emblem of care.

sentences.zh: 中兴但以郎兼，事讫罢，又省车、户、骑凡三将，如淳曰：「主车曰车郎，主户卫曰户郎。」

translations.literal: At restoration only gentlemen doubled the posts, dismissed when the affair ended; also eliminated were the three generals of chariots, household guard, and cavalry. Ru Chun said: "Those mastering chariots were called chariot gentlemen; those mastering household guard were called household gentlemen."
translations.idiomatic: After the restoration gentlemen temporarily doubled these posts and were dismissed when duty ended; the chariot, household, and cavalry commanders were cut. Ru Chun glossed chariot gentlemen and household gentlemen."

translations.literal: Also the Director of Feathered Forest.
translations.idiomatic: The Feathered Forest director remained.

translations.literal: Minister of the Guard, minister, one person, at fully ranked two thousand bushels.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of the Guard: one minister at fully ranked two thousand bushels.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：掌宫门卫士，宫中徼循事。

translations.literal: Original commentary: he holds palace-gate guardsmen and patrol affairs within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: He commands the gate guards and palace patrols.

translations.literal: One assistant, comparable to one thousand bushels.
translations.idiomatic: He has one assistant at one thousand bushels equivalent.

sentences.zh: 公车司马令一人，六百石。

translations.literal: Director of the public-carriage and horse marshal, one person, six hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: One director of the public carriage gate and horse marshal at six hundred bushels.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：掌宫南阙门，凡吏民上章，四方贡献，及征诣公车者。

translations.literal: Original commentary: he holds the southern gate tower of the palace; all officials and commoners submitting memorials, regional tribute, and those summoned to the public carriage.
translations.idiomatic: He controls the palace’s southern portal for memorials, tribute convoys, and men summoned to the “public carriage” audience.

translations.literal: One assistant and one commandant each.
translations.idiomatic: He has one assistant and one commandant.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：丞选晓讳，掌知非法。

translations.literal: Original commentary: the assistant is chosen for knowledge of taboo names and masters knowing what is unlawful.
translations.idiomatic: The assistant must know imperial taboos and flag irregular petitions.

translations.literal: The commandant masters gate-tower troops and prohibitions, guarding against the extraordinary.
translations.idiomatic: The commandant enforces armed watch at the tower and bars emergencies.

sentences.zh: 南宫卫士令一人，六百石。

translations.literal: Director of Southern Palace guardsmen, one person, six hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: One director of Southern Palace guards at six hundred bushels.

translations.literal: Original commentary: he holds Southern Palace guardsmen.
translations.idiomatic: He commands the Southern Palace guard detail.

translations.literal: One assistant.
translations.idiomatic: He has one assistant.

sentences.zh: 北宫卫士令一人，六百石。

translations.literal: Director of Northern Palace guardsmen, one person, six hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: One director of Northern Palace guards at six hundred bushels.

translations.literal: Original commentary: he holds Northern Palace guardsmen.
translations.idiomatic: He commands the Northern Palace guard detail.

translations.literal: One assistant.
translations.idiomatic: He has one assistant.

sentences.zh: 左右都候各一人，六百石。

translations.literal: Left and right metropolitan patrol commanders, one each, six hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: Left and right metropolitan patrol commanders at six hundred bushels each.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：主剑戟士，徼循宫及天子有所收考。

translations.literal: Original commentary: they command halberdiers, patrol the palace, and when the Son of Heaven has someone to seize or interrogate.
translations.idiomatic: They lead halberd guards on palace rounds and make arrests when the throne orders an inquiry.

translations.literal: One assistant each.
translations.idiomatic: Each command has one assistant.

sentences.zh: 宫掖门，每门司马一人，比千石。

translations.literal: For palace and harem gates, each gate has one major, comparable to one thousand bushels.
translations.idiomatic: Every inner gate posts one major at one thousand bushels equivalent.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：南宫南屯司马，主平城门；

translations.literal: Original commentary: South Regiment Major of the Southern Palace masters Pingcheng Gate;
translations.idiomatic: The Southern Palace’s south camp major holds Pingcheng Gate;

sentences.zh: 汉官曰：「员吏九人，卫士百二人。」

translations.literal: The Offices of Han says: "Nine staff and one hundred two guards."
translations.idiomatic: The Offices of Han lists nine clerks and 102 guards."

sentences.zh: 古今注曰建武十三年九月，初开此门。

translations.literal: Notes Ancient and Modern says: in the ninth month of the thirteenth year of Jianwu, this gate was first opened.
translations.idiomatic: Notes Ancient and Modern dates the gate's first opening to the ninth month of Jianwu 13.

translations.literal: Palace Gate Azure Dragon Commandant masters the east gate;
translations.idiomatic: The Azure Dragon palace gate commandant holds the east gate;

sentences.zh: 案雒阳宫门名为苍龙阙门。

translations.literal: On investigation the Luoyang palace gate is named Azure Dragon Tower Gate.
translations.idiomatic: Luoyang's east palace gate was called the Azure Dragon Tower Gate.

sentences.zh: 汉官曰：「员吏六人，卫士四十人。」

translations.literal: The Offices of Han says: "Six staff and forty guards."
translations.idiomatic: The Offices of Han gives the post six clerks and forty guards."

translations.literal: Black Tortoise Major masters Black Tortoise Gate;
translations.idiomatic: the Black Tortoise major holds Black Tortoise Gate;

translations.literal: North Regiment Major masters the north gate;
translations.idiomatic: the north camp major holds the north gate;

sentences.zh: 北宫朱爵司马，主南掖门；

translations.literal: Vermilion Sparrow Major of the Northern Palace masters the south harem gate;
translations.idiomatic: the Northern Palace’s Vermilion Sparrow major holds the south harem portal;

translations.literal: Dawn-clarity Major masters the east gate;
translations.idiomatic: the Dawn-clarity major holds the east inner gate;

sentences.zh: 朔平司马，主北门：凡七门。

translations.literal: Pacified-north Major masters the north gate: in all seven gates.
translations.idiomatic: and the Pacified-north major holds the north inner gate—seven gates in all.

sentences.zh: 凡居宫中者，皆有口籍于门之所属。

translations.literal: All who dwell within the palace have mouth tallies registered with the gate to which they belong.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone quartered inside carries a mouth tally filed with the gate that controls his passage.

sentences.zh: 宫名两字，为铁印文符，案省符乃内之。

translations.literal: The palace name of two characters is an iron-seal text tally; they inspect the tally and only then admit them.
translations.idiomatic: Each two-character gate name is cast on an iron tally; the seal must match before entry is granted.

sentences.zh: 胡广曰：「符用木，长尺二寸，铁印以符之。」

translations.literal: Hu Guang said: "The tally is of wood, one foot two inches long; an iron seal authenticates the tally."
translations.idiomatic: Hu Guang noted that the wooden tally was one foot two inches long and authenticated by an iron seal."

sentences.zh: 若外人以事当入，本官长史为封棨传；

translations.literal: If an outsider must enter on business, the chief clerk of his home office seals a tally pass;
translations.idiomatic: Official visitors must carry a wooden tally pass sealed by their agency's chief clerk;

sentences.zh: 其有官位，出入令御者言其官。

translations.literal: If they have official rank, going out and in they order the charioteer to announce their office.
translations.idiomatic: Ranked officials declare their title to the coachman when passing in or out.

translations.literal: Those on the right belong to the Minister of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: The offices at right belong to the Minister of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：中兴省旅贲令，卫士一人丞。

translations.literal: Original commentary: at restoration the Director of Rapid Escort was eliminated; the guard office has one assistant.
translations.idiomatic: The restoration abolished the Director of Rapid Escort and left each guard bureau with a single assistant.

sentences.zh: 汉官目录曰：「右三卿，太尉所部。」

translations.literal: The Han Offices Catalogue says: "The three ministers at right belong to the Grand Commandant."
translations.idiomatic: The Han Offices Catalogue places the three ministries at right under the Grand Commandant."

translations.literal: Minister Coachman, minister, one person, at fully ranked two thousand bushels.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister Coachman: one minister at fully ranked two thousand bushels.

translations.literal: Original commentary: he holds chariots and horses.
translations.idiomatic: He is steward of the imperial stables and carriages.

sentences.zh: 天子每出，奏驾上卤簿，用大驾则执御。

translations.literal: Whenever the Son of Heaven goes out, he presents the chariot and ascends the guard of honor; when the grand chariot is used then he holds the reins.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor travels he arranges the chariot train and, for the grand progress, takes the reins himself.

sentences.zh: 汉官曰：「员吏七十人，其七人四科，一人二百石，文学八人百石，六人斗食，七人佐，六人骑吏，三人假佐，三十一人学事，一人官医。」

translations.literal: The Offices of Han says: "Seventy staff: seven in four grades, one at two hundred bushels, eight literary officers at one hundred bushels, six at dou-food rank, seven assistants, six cavalry clerks, three acting assistants, thirty-one student clerks, one court physician."
translations.idiomatic: The Offices of Han lists seventy staff: seven graded officers, one at two hundred bushels, eight literary clerks, six dou-food clerks, seven assistants, six cavalry clerks, three acting assistants, thirty-one student clerks, and one court physician."

translations.literal: One assistant, comparable to one thousand bushels.
translations.idiomatic: He has one assistant at one thousand bushels equivalent.

translations.literal: Director of the workshop, one person, six hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: One director of the imperial workshop at six hundred bushels.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：主作兵器弓弩刀铠之属，成则传执金吾入武库，及主织绶诸杂工。

translations.literal: Original commentary: he masters making weapons, crossbows, blades, armor, and the like; when finished they are passed to the Commandant of the Metropolitan Guard for entry into the armory, and he also masters weaving ribbons and various crafts.
translations.idiomatic: He manufactured arms and armor, delivered finished goods to the metropolitan guard for the armory, and oversaw ribbon weaving and other crafts.

translations.literal: The Offices of Han says: "One hundred nine staff."
translations.idiomatic: The Offices of Han lists 109 clerks."

translations.literal: Left and right assistants, one each.
translations.idiomatic: He has left and right assistants.

translations.literal: Director of the chariot office, one person, six hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: One director of the chariot depot at six hundred bushels.

translations.literal: Original commentary: he masters all chariots of the imperial equipage.
translations.idiomatic: He maintains every vehicle in the imperial garage.

translations.literal: One assistant.
translations.idiomatic: He has one assistant.

translations.literal: Director of the Weiyang stable, one person, six hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: One director of the Weiyang stable at six hundred bushels.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：主乘舆及厩中诸马。

translations.literal: Original commentary: he masters the imperial equipage and all horses in the stable.
translations.idiomatic: He tends the emperor's carriage horses and the rest of the Weiyang herd.

sentences.zh: 汉官曰：「员吏七十人，卒驺二十人。」

translations.literal: The Offices of Han says: "Seventy staff and twenty mounted runners."
translations.idiomatic: The Offices of Han lists seventy clerks and twenty mounted runners."

translations.literal: Assistant director of the Changle stable, one person.
translations.idiomatic: One assistant director serves the Changle Palace stable.

sentences.zh: 汉官曰：「员吏十五人，率驺二十人。

translations.literal: The Offices of Han says: "Fifteen staff and twenty mounted runners.
translations.idiomatic: The Offices of Han says: "Fifteen clerks and twenty mounted runners,

sentences.zh: 苜蓿苑官田所一人守之。」

translations.literal: One man guards the alfalfa park official fields."
translations.idiomatic: and one warden for the alfalfa park fields."

translations.literal: Those on the right belong to the Minister Coachman.
translations.idiomatic: The offices at right report to the Minister Coachman.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：旧有六厩，皆六百石令，前书曰，有大厩、未央、家马三令，各五丞一尉。

translations.literal: Original commentary: formerly there were six stables, each with a six-hundred-bushel director; the Former Book says there were directors of the great stable, Weiyang, and imperial horses—three directors, each with five assistants and one commandant.
translations.idiomatic: Western Han ran six stables under six-hundred-bushel directors; the Former Book names great, Weiyang, and imperial horse stables, each with five deputies and a commandant.

sentences.zh: 又车府、路軨、骑马、骏马四令丞。

translations.literal: Also the chariot office, road-chariot, riding horse, and fine horse—four directors and assistants.
translations.idiomatic: There were also directors for the chariot depot, road chariots, riding horses, and fine horses.

sentences.zh: 晋灼曰：「六厩名也，主马万匹。」

translations.literal: Jin Zhuo said: "These were the names of the six stables, mastering ten thousand horses."
translations.idiomatic: Jin Zhuo explained that the six names denoted stables keeping as many as ten thousand horses.

translations.literal: At restoration they were reduced and only one stable was set.
translations.idiomatic: The restored court kept only one stable.

sentences.zh: 后置左骏令、厩，别主乘舆御马，后或并省。

translations.literal: Later they set up a left fine-horse director and stable, separately mastering imperial carriage horses; later these too were sometimes merged and cut.
translations.idiomatic: Later a separate left fine-horse stable was added for imperial carriage mounts, then sometimes abolished again.

sentences.zh: 又有牧师范，皆令官，主养马，分在河西六郡界中，中兴皆省，唯汉阳有流马菀，但以羽林郎监领。

translations.literal: Moreover there were pastoral zones and stud farms, each with a director official, mastering horse breeding, distributed within the borders of the six western commanderies; at restoration all were eliminated; only Hanyang retained a “flowing horse” park, supervised solely by a Feathered Forest gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Pastoral officials once bred remounts across six western commanderies until the restoration abolished them; only Hanyang’s “flowing horse” breeding ground survived, overseen by a Feathered Forest officer.

translations.literal: Minister of Justice, minister, one person, at fully ranked two thousand bushels.
translations.idiomatic: The Minister of Justice: one minister at fully ranked two thousand bushels.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：掌平狱，奏当所应。

translations.literal: Original commentary: he holds leveling of prisons and memorializing what judgments should be.
translations.idiomatic: He supervises criminal justice and memorializes the appropriate sentences.

sentences.zh: 凡郡国谳疑罪，皆处当以报。

translations.literal: For doubtful crimes in commanderies and kingdoms, all are judged and reported with the appropriate sentence.
translations.idiomatic: Doubtful cases from the provinces were decided and reported with recommended sentences.

translations.literal: Hu Guang said: "Yan means to verify."
translations.idiomatic: Hu Guang glossed yan as "to verify."

sentences.zh: 汉官曰：「员吏百四十人，其十一人四科，十六人二百石廷吏，文学十六人百石，十三人狱史，二十七人佐，二十六人骑吏，三十人假佐，一人官医。」

translations.literal: The Offices of Han says: "One hundred forty staff: eleven in four grades, sixteen two-hundred-bushel court clerks, sixteen literary officers at one hundred bushels, thirteen prison clerks, twenty-seven assistants, twenty-six cavalry clerks, thirty acting assistants, one court physician."
translations.idiomatic: The Offices of Han lists 140 staff including graded officers, court clerks, literary clerks, prison clerks, assistants, cavalry clerks, acting assistants, and one court physician."

translations.literal: One rectifying judge and one left superintendent each.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry staffs one rectifying judge and one left prison superintendent.

translations.literal: Left leveling officer, one person, six hundred bushels.
translations.idiomatic: One left “leveling” officer at six hundred bushels.

translations.literal: Original commentary: he holds leveling judgments in edict prisons.
translations.idiomatic: He adjudicates cases held in the emperor’s special prisons.

translations.literal: Those on the right belong to the Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: The offices at right fall under the Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：孝武帝以下，置中都官狱二十六所，各令长名世祖中兴皆省，唯廷尉及雒阳有诏狱。

translations.literal: Original commentary: from Emperor Xiaowu downward, twenty-six capital-office prisons were established, each with a director or chief by name; at the Founding Ancestor’s restoration all were eliminated; only the Minister of Justice and Luoyang retained edict prisons.
translations.idiomatic: From Emperor Wu on the capital ran twenty-six separate prison bureaus, each with its own warden; Guangwu abolished them, leaving only the Minister of Justice’s jails and Luoyang’s imperial prison.

sentences.zh: 蔡质汉仪曰：「正月旦，石官朝贺，光禄勋刘嘉、廷尉赵世各辞不能朝，高赐举奏：『皆以被病笃困，空文武之位，阙上卿之赞，既无忠信断金之用，而有败礼伤化之尤，不谨不敬！

translations.literal: Cai Zhi's Han Ceremonies says: "On the first day of the first month, when stone officials attended court congratulations, Minister of the Household Liu Jia and Commandant of Justice Zhao Shi each pleaded illness and could not attend. Gao Ci memorialized and impeached them: 'Both claim grave illness, leaving civil and military posts empty and lacking the support of upper ministers; they are useless for loyal, faithful solidarity and are guilty of the grave fault of damaging ritual and harming custom—negligent and disrespectful!
translations.idiomatic: Cai Zhi's Han Ceremonies records: "On New Year's day Liu Jia and Zhao Shi pleaded illness and stayed away; Gao Ci impeached them for deserting their posts and harming court ritual, declaring them negligent and disrespectful:

sentences.zh: 请廷尉治嘉罪，河南尹治世罪。』

translations.literal: I ask that the Commandant of Justice try Jia's crime and the Governor of Henan try Shi's crime.
translations.idiomatic: he asked that Jia be tried by the commandant of justice and Shi by the governor of Henan

sentences.zh: 议以世掌廷尉，故转属他官。」

translations.literal: Because Shi headed the Commandant of Justice, the case was transferred to another office."
translations.idiomatic: though Shi's own office required transferring the case."

sentences.zh: 大鸿胪，卿一人，中二千石。

translations.literal: Grand Herald, minister, one person, at fully ranked two thousand bushels.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Herald: one minister at fully ranked two thousand bushels.

sentences.zh: 周礼「象胥」，干宝注曰今鸿胪。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou "image interpreters"; Gan Bao's commentary says this is today's Grand Herald.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhou "image interpreters" were, in Gan Bao's gloss, the Grand Herald of later times.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：掌诸侯及四方归义蛮夷。

translations.literal: Original commentary: he holds feudal lords and barbarians of the four quarters who have submitted in righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He receives feudal princes and foreign peoples who have pledged allegiance.

sentences.zh: 其郊庙行礼，赞导，请行事，既可，以命群司。

translations.literal: At suburban and temple rites he assists and leads, requests the carrying out of affairs; once approved, by this he orders the host of offices.
translations.idiomatic: At suburban and ancestral rites he prompts the liturgy, seeks permission to proceed, then instructs the ministries once the emperor assents.

sentences.zh: 诸王入朝，当郊迎，典其礼仪。

translations.literal: When kings enter court, he should meet them at the suburban altar and holds their ritual protocol.
translations.idiomatic: When princes come to audience he meets them at the suburban station and directs their ceremonial approach.

sentences.zh: 及郡国上计，匡四方来，亦属焉。

translations.literal: And when commanderies and kingdoms present annual accounts, and correctors from the four quarters arrive, these also attach to him.
translations.idiomatic: Regional accounting missions and inspectors from abroad likewise report through his ministry.

translations.literal: When imperial sons are invested as kings, he assists in presenting the seal and ribbons.
translations.idiomatic: When a son of the throne is enfeoffed as a king, he presents the seal and sash on the emperor’s behalf.

sentences.zh: 及拜诸侯、诸侯嗣子及四方夷狄封者，台下鸿胪召拜之。

translations.literal: And when investing feudal lords, heirs of feudal lords, and those from the four quarters barbarians who are to be enfeoffed, below the terrace the Grand Herald summons them for the investiture.
translations.idiomatic: Investitures of feudal lords, their heirs, and foreign rulers summoned for enfeoffment are conducted below the hall steps under the Grand Herald’s call.

sentences.zh: 王薨则使吊之，及拜王嗣。

translations.literal: When a king dies he dispatches someone to offer condolences, and for investing the king’s successor.
translations.idiomatic: On a king’s death he sends condolences; he also oversees the heir’s investiture.

translations.literal: One assistant.
translations.idiomatic: He has one assistant.

translations.literal: Comparable to one thousand bushels.
translations.idiomatic: That assistant ranks at one thousand bushels equivalent.

sentences.zh: 大行令一人，六百石，本注曰：主诸郎。

translations.literal: Director of grand processions, one person, six hundred bushels; original commentary: he commands the various gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: One director of grand processions at six hundred bushels, in charge of the ministry’s gentlemen.

translations.literal: One assistant.
translations.idiomatic: He has one assistant.

translations.literal: Rite-regulating gentlemen, forty-seven persons.
translations.idiomatic: Forty-seven rite-regulating gentlemen assist at state ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 汉官曰：「其四人四科，五人二百石，文学五人百石，九人斗食，六人佐，六人学事，十二人守学事。」

translations.literal: The Offices of Han says: "Four men in four grades, five at two hundred bushels, five literary officers at one hundred bushels, nine at dou-food rank, six assistants, six student clerks, twelve supervising student clerks."
translations.idiomatic: The Offices of Han lists four graded officers, five at two hundred bushels, five literary clerks at one hundred, nine dou-food staff, six assistants, six student clerks, and twelve supervising student clerks."

sentences.zh: 东观书曰：「主斋祠傧赞九宾。

translations.literal: The Eastern Lodge Record says: "They preside over fasting sacrifices, protocol, and assisting the nine guests.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Lodge Record says: "They manage fasting rites and guest protocol,

sentences.zh: 又有公室，主调中都官斗食以下，功次相补。」

translations.literal: There is also a public office that coordinates capital officials at dou-food rank and below, filling posts by merit in order."
translations.idiomatic: with a separate office ranking capital clerks below dou-food grade by merit."

sentences.zh: 案卢植礼注曰：「大行郎亦如谒者，兼举形貌。」

translations.literal: Lu Zhi's Rites commentary says: "Grand procession gentlemen, like receptionists, also report on physical appearance."
translations.idiomatic: Lu Zhi noted that grand procession gentlemen, like receptionists, also assessed appearance.

translations.literal: Those on the right belong to the Grand Herald.
translations.idiomatic: The offices at right belong to the Grand Herald.

sentences.zh: 本注曰：承秦有典属国，别主四方夷狄朝贡侍子，成帝时省并大鸿胪。

translations.literal: Original commentary: inheriting Qin there was a director of dependent states, separately mastering the four quarters' barbarians' court tribute and hostage sons; in Emperor Cheng's time it was eliminated and merged into the Grand Herald.
translations.idiomatic: Qin's office of dependent states once handled foreign tribute and hostage princes until Emperor Cheng folded it into the Grand Herald.

sentences.zh: 中兴省驿官、别火二令、丞，如淳曰：「汉仪注：『别火，狱令官，主治改火事。』」

translations.literal: At restoration the relay-office and separate-fire directors and assistants were eliminated. Ru Chun said: "The Han Ceremonies commentary: 'Separate Fire was a prison directorate, mastering the seasonal change of hearth fires.'"
translations.idiomatic: The restoration cut the relay and Separate Fire directorates. Ru Chun glossed Separate Fire as the prison office that managed the ritual change of hearth fires."

sentences.zh: 及郡邸长、丞，但令郎治郡邸。

translations.literal: As for commandery hostel chiefs and assistants, only gentlemen were ordered to manage commandery hostels.
translations.idiomatic: Commandery hostel chiefs and assistants were reduced so that gentlemen alone ran the hostels.

sentences.zh: 汉官目录曰：「右三官，司徒所部。」

translations.literal: The Han Offices Catalogue says: "The three offices at right belong to the Minister of Education."
translations.idiomatic: The Han Offices Catalogue lists the three offices at right under the Minister of Education."
